input.command:
python -c "
import pandas as pd,numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
d=pd.read_csv('spectrum.csv');x=d.shift_cm1.values;y=d.intensity.values
m=(x>60)&(x<260)
def f(x,a,c,w,a2,c2,w2,a3,c3,w3,b,s):
    g=lambda a,c,w:a*np.exp(-4*np.log(2)*((x-c)/w)**2)
    return g(a,c,w)+g(a2,c2,w2)+g(a3,c3,w3)+b+s*(x-150)
p0=[12000,181.4,8,600,137,20,500,167,12,6500,0]
p,cv=curve_fit(f,x[m],y[m],p0,maxfev=20000);e=np.sqrt(np.diag(cv))
print(np.round(p,1));print(np.round(e,1))
# local 72 check
mm=(x>60)&(x<85);print(y[mm].mean(),y[(x>90)&(x<110)].mean())
"

python -c "
import pandas as pd,numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
d=pd.read_csv('spectrum.csv');x=d.shift_cm1.values;y=d.intensity.values
m=(x>60)&(x<260)
def f(x,a,c,w,a2,c2,w2,a3,c3,w3,b,s):
    g=lambda a,c,w:a*np.exp(-4*np.log(2)*((x-c)/w)**2)
    return g(a,c,w)+g(a2,c2,w2)+g(a3,c3,w3)+b+s*(x-150)
p0=[12000,181.4,8,600,137,20,500,167,12,6500,0]
p,cv=curve_fit(f,x[m],y[m],p0,maxfev=20000);e=np.sqrt(np.diag(cv))
print(np.round(p,1));print(np.round(e,1))
# local 72 check
mm=(x>60)&(x<85);print(y[mm].mean(),y[(x>90)&(x<110)].mean())
"

candidates.evidence: The only strong line is at 181.4 cm-1 (FWHM about 8 cm-1). A weak, broad feature sits near 140 cm-1. The strong line is the closest match to the A1g(2) mode, and the 140 cm-1 feature is the closest match to Eg(2). Both lie 7-9 cm-1 above the usual positions (about 174 and 131 cm-1), and A1g(1) near 72 cm-1 is not seen. Only the 532 nm laser, a Raman spectrum and a layered-material context support this identification.
Its main modes are Eg(2) near 103, A1g(2) near 134 and A1g(1) near 62 cm-1. None of these match a dominant line at 181 cm-1.
It has its strongest lines near 190 and 210 cm-1 and a broad band around 150-160 cm-1. The single sharp line at 181 with no companion near 210 does not fit.
Its modes are near 69, 112 and 165 cm-1, so the 181 cm-1 line is 16 cm-1 too high.

The 181 cm-1 line is about 7 cm-1 above the usual Bi2Se3 A1g(2) position. The Eg(2) hump is about 9 cm-1 high. I cannot say whether this comes from strain, a different composition, calibration offset or another material.
A1g(1) near 72 cm-1 is absent. This could be because the signal-to-noise ratio is low or because of the sample, and I cannot tell which.
The data are not angle-resolved, so the polarization pattern of each mode is unknown. The irreps are assigned only by position.
The noise is high, so weak features such as the 140 cm-1 hump and any broad features above 250 cm-1 cannot be assigned. Peaks found in the noise above 250 cm-1 were not treated as real.
No Si peak at 520.7 cm-1 is detectable. The substrate is not given in the metadata, and it cannot be identified from these data.
Layer number, doping and strain cannot be quantified from a single unpolarized spectrum.
